10 اِسْتَرْوَحَ , said of a branch, (Msb, TA,) It became shaken by the wind: (TA:) or it inclined from side to side. (Msb.) ―
-b2- See also 1, near the beginning of the paragraph; and see اِسْتَرْوَحْتُ إِلَى حَدِيثِهِ, and استراح الى حديثه, in the former part of the same paragraph. ―
-b3- Also, (K,) and استراح, (S, A, Msb, K,) [which latter is the more common in this sense,] and ↓ ارتاح , (TA,) and sometimes ↓ اراح , q. v., (Msb,) [and ↓ تروّح , as quasi-pass. of رَوَّحَ عَنْهُ or بِهِ,] said of a hired man, (Msb,) [and of any man,] He found, or experienced, rest, or ease; [was, or became, at rest, or at ease; rested;] (S, * A, * Msb, * K;) مِنْهُ [from him, or it], (A,) and بِهِ [by means of it]; (Msb;) from الرَّاحَةُ; (S;) quasi-pass. of أَرَحْتُهُ,
(A, Msb,) and of أَرَاحَهُ ٱللّٰهُ. (S.) ―
-b4- استروح إِلَيْهِ (accord. to the S and K, but in other lexicons استراح, TA) He trusted to, or relied upon, him, or it, and became quiet, or easy, in mind. (S, K, TA.) ―
-b5- See also 1, in the last quarter of the paragraph, in seven places. ＝
-A2- استروح المَطَرُ الشَّجَرَ The rain revived the trees. (L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
